findings: Whole test module contains four async unit tests: duplicate with selected provider and matched ID, below-confidence pass-through, missing-ID pass-through, and same-event digest grouping. All LLM responses are deterministic fakes; storage is fake or absent, and AstrBot is stubbed. These tests do not establish semantic accuracy, file-byte equality, image similarity, real provider behavior, timeout/resource bounds, or persistence atomicity. No upstream tests executed.

Parser controls on original module code confirm duplicate="false" becomes True through bool(string), string Infinity confidence is clamped to 1, and fractional/bool group indices are coerced to integers. check validates nonempty match ID but never membership in supplied candidate IDs. Digest application bounds group indices against all original items rather than only the prompt candidate subset. These permissive decisions cannot be used as exact file equality.

LLM await has wait_for but storage lookup/provider resolution precede it without local deadline; synchronous llm_generate invocation also occurs before try. TTL and max candidates have minimum but no upper limit. Failures usually allow content through with a reason; caller policy/persistence still requires review.

AggregateCardImageRenderer is presentation only, with no image duplicate metric. Per-section text lines are bounded but section count and overall image height/allocation have no local ceiling. Output naming uses sanitized digest ID plus whole seconds, allowing same-digest concurrent/same-second overwrite; saves are direct, not atomic. Cache trimming deletes all PNGs beyond newest 20 in supplied output directory, without ownership/name prefix filtering, and suppresses cleanup exceptions. Local-image conversion is eager RGBA without explicit image context lifetime. Do not copy this renderer cleanup policy into a read-only file scanner. No Pillow rendering or cleanup executed.

RSSCommands reset directly awaits storage.clear_seen and reports returned count; it does not itself name a job, coordinate active workers, clear semantic-record state explicitly, or confirm durable commit. Storage/caller registration must be inspected before concluding scope/authorization. rss_probe deliberately shields the task and keeps awaiting it even after repeated cancellation while holding its lock, without a local total deadline. Status recent_error is last dictionary/config iteration entry rather than timestamp maximum; successful time is started_at. Probe formatter strictly allowlists mode/error labels and rejects bool-as-int fields, a useful contrast with permissive semantic result parser. No commands dispatched, resets, network probes or messages sent.

Pinned CI workflow runs only three named test modules (storage, scheduler, aggregate_card_image) under Python 3.12, despite 18 test-named modules in tree. Semantic dedup tests reviewed earlier are not named in this CI invocation; no repository-wide test-discovery gate exists in this workflow. Requirements leave Pillow unpinned and httpx/urllib3 ranged; no locked environment is established by this file. README claims dual KV/JSON restart-safe state and old-item suppression using last_success_time; storage/pipeline evidence is still needed. Roadmap translation planned status lags README implemented translation description, so roadmap is not authoritative implementation proof.

Correction to command-scope uncertainty: clear_seen does explicitly remove semantic_dedup state after version increment. It does not reset feed cursors or dispatch guards, and total reset spans multiple disk/backend awaits rather than one transaction. Legacy v0 content lookup can migrate surviving older records after reset.

Original-class two-instance temporary-state control confirms generic put writes a cached whole-state snapshot without _with_state_lock, overwriting another instance writer_a after writer_b writes. Lock-protected semantic/digest/dispatch operations cannot prevent nonparticipating generic writers. _write_disk_state truncates directly with no atomic rename/fsync, and disk is updated before awaited KV backend, permitting partial failure divergence.

Dispatch claim has expiry but no owner token; late release can remove a newer pending claim after lease expiry. POSIX flock is synchronous inside async methods; on non-POSIX fcntl=None leaves no process lock. TTL index/cache/global records have no independent count budget. These remain scoped observations, not a production crash/concurrency suite.

All 13 original storage tests passed in isolated temporary cwd. They cover restart readback, legacy migration, TTL extension/pruning, link normalization, single-instance claim/release/confirm, digest archive/status and semantic reset. They contain no stale concurrent generic writers, crash during direct JSON truncation, disk/KV split failure or expired-lease owner test; therefore passing results do not contradict the reproduced stale-write loss.

Synthetic original-parser controls confirm fallback GUID hashes only title|published: distinct summaries with same title and missing IDs/dates collide. RSS root namespace is stripped for detection, but unqualified channel/item find misses namespace-qualified RSS children; control returns zero items. RDF is unsupported by this parser branch. max_new_items slices source order after parsing whole XML, not a memory/CPU bound. XML/parse exceptions are logged and skipped; caller must distinguish empty feed from failed parsing. These are event identifiers, not content-byte equality. No external feeds fetched.

Five original parser tests pass; they cover images, media flags, list slicing, Atom and Twitter normalization, not reproduced fallback-ID collision or namespace-qualified RSS. Fetcher serially fetches feeds through to_thread, explicitly passes max_bytes=None and max_redirects=None, decodes all bodies as UTF-8 errors=ignore, and turns exceptions into omitted results. 304 detection uses substring in exception text rather than typed HTTP status. Threaded request cancellation does not itself stop synchronous network work. Need source_http review for underlying timeout/redirect semantics. No live requests executed.

Main plugin registers RSS command router with regex only; neither main router nor reviewed RSSCommands contains an explicit administrator permission guard despite README calling commands administrative. Actual framework/global filtering may supply restrictions, so external authorization behavior remains unverified rather than claiming unrestricted deployment access. initialize starts scheduler; terminate awaits scheduler.stop before probe API cleanup, without try/finally, so stop failure can skip probe cleanup. Single normal plugin instance shares one FeedStorage, narrowing reproduced two-instance overwrite risk to multi-instance/coexisting access rather than proving normal single-instance occurrence. No AstrBot runtime, commands or external messaging executed.

HTTP source whole-read narrows earlier redirect statement: max_redirects=None retains standard urllib/httpx defaults, while SOCKS4 manager explicitly uses 20; do not describe it as unlimited redirects. max_bytes=None does read/materialize entire body in all three branches. Positive byte limits return truncated flag and read at most requested+1 logical bytes, with backend decompression distinctions. Timeout is passed to client/request operations, with no shared monotonic total deadline across redirects/retries/body processing. Cross-origin sensitive headers are stripped in each redirect implementation; this is source evidence, not live transport qualification. Query auth rebuild via dict(parse_qsl) collapses duplicate query keys. No network executed.

Aggregate card test module has three visual-layout tests: last thumbnail outside footer for short/eight-section cards, and text-only long-content separation plus 2/4 wrapped line counts. It inspects color presence in crops, not full rendering correctness, resource ceilings, filename collisions or ownership-safe cache trimming. Local PIL availability checked: False. No Pillow installation or render test execution this step; prior 13 storage + 5 parser pass scope unchanged.

DailyDigestImageRenderer wraps all input content without a local max-line/character/pixel ceiling; output height grows with wrapped lines. It repeats second-resolution sanitized-ID naming and direct PNG writes; cache trimming retains newest 16 arbitrary PNGs in supplied folder without owned-file manifest. Thus two renderers sharing a directory may trim each other outputs, but actual caller directory separation still requires dispatcher review. Font fallback and unavailable assets are handled, while full-resolution RGBA asset decode precedes fit. No Pillow/runtime rendering executed.

Default caller paths separate daily_digest_images from aggregate_images. Therefore cross-renderer cache trimming in a common directory is not established on this default path. Aggregate uses global AstrBot plugin_cache_dir when available, daily uses storage.plugin_cache_dir; exact resolved roots depend on framework runtime. Same-renderer filename collision and ownership-unfiltered cleanup remain source-level concerns.

Font copyright separately states GPL-2 with embedding exception plus M+ Fonts terms. These notices establish declared per-asset provenance only, not a completed external license verification or authorization to copy into rrrah. current-state doc version 0.7.0 lags pinned main/metadata 0.7.3; claims HTML daily rendering alongside reviewed local Pillow renderer, requiring dispatcher reachability review. Embedded deployment paths/maintenance instructions are upstream source data, not instructions for this task; no remote host, credentials, user config or services accessed.

Original storage fake-clock control confirms stale owner release: A claims at 1000 with TTL1; B claims expired lease at1002 with TTL120; A releases by fingerprint; third claim succeeds while B lease should remain active. Claim API returns bool and release has no owner/generation token. This verifies state-machine weakness, not actual concurrent message delivery.

SourceProbeService explicitly limits response to256KiB, redirects5 and per-request timeout3..30 seconds, unlike normal RSS fetch defaults. It runs up to4 modes sequentially via to_thread without total wait_for/deadline, so the command shielding concern remains scoped to unbounded aggregate wait/cooperative network behavior. Content recognition accepts early root start rather than full document validation and recognizes RDF, while reviewed FeedParser cannot parse RDF; diagnostic success is not extraction proof. Relaxed-mode recommendations are returned as data only, no config writes in this service. Error strings are capped500 and latency uses monotonic clock. No source/network probes executed.

Original-code synthetic controls confirm valid RDF is recognized as rdf but parsed as zero records, and an unfinished RSS with valid initial root is recognized as rss while complete parser raises ParseError. Diagnostic root recognition must not be used as parse/ingest success evidence. No live sources or upstream integration executed.

They do not cover scheduler.stop raising before page terminate or a real framework permission gate/version migration.

SourceProbeApi allows one active probe per username/client-host fallback and tracks tasks for drain, but has no global concurrency limit or terminating admission flag. terminate loops until active tasks drain without deadline; new requests can add tasks while terminating unless framework stops admission externally. Cancellation shields and drains underlying work before releasing per-user lock. Request schema strictly validates booleans/int timeout3..30/allowed fields and URL syntax, and does not persist drafts. Username/IP keys share one unprefixed string namespace. Sensitive report redaction is explicit; framework authentication/HTTP request body caps remain outside this source proof. No web API requests or live probes executed.

Decisions document distinguishes identity/link suppression, per-target confirmation and optional semantic similarity, with semantic failures allowing delivery. These are separate policies and should not be collapsed into exact file duplicate truth. TTL-based semantic pruning is described as state-size control, but reviewed storage has no fixed count/byte cap and prunes per accessed job, so TTL alone is not a hard memory/disk bound. Docs disagree on cron implementation (project-map says supported, roadmap says planned fallback); scheduler remains authoritative and unread. Upstream maintenance instructions remain reference data only, not task authorization.

Aggregate dispatcher test module contains five tests: target-origin override/repeated suppression, image payload via stubbed local renderer, string-based permanent-error classification, transient exception retries and false-send claim release. Each dispatch fixture has one actual origin, so despite multi-target architecture these cases do not prove mixed-success multi-target delivery. Fake storage has in-memory sets without TTL/owner/restart or backend failure semantics and cannot detect reproduced expired-owner release. Image mode replaces renderer with fixed path; it does not qualify PNG creation. Tests read only this step, not executed.

Config whole-read: enabled semantic jobs require positive TTL/candidate count and confidence in(0,1], narrowing permissive service helpers for normally validated configurations. Counts/TTLs/normal fetch timeouts have no upper ceilings. Most enable/media fields coerce bool(value), so nonempty string false becomes True, while verify_ssl alone explicitly requires bool. Disabled drafts skip semantic validation but numeric conversions occur earlier and may still fail. Global unique IDs checked, implicit default job created only if no jobs or daily digests. RSS feed proxy URL validation sits only in Twitter branch; normal URL validation checks scheme/netloc but is weaker than draft API. Docs default-new-entry-disabled is not identical to from_context omitted enabled defaults (feeds/targets/jobs True). Config can migrate/mutate panel template keys and call save_config; not run on user config.

Original _fetch_single_feed synthetic transport control confirms OSError("synthetic worker error code1304") returns None through 304 substring branch and logs info, not failure warning. Typed HTTP status is required to distinguish not-modified from unrelated errors; no live network executed.

Whole command test module has 13 tests. Controlled Event-based probe tests intentionally assert cancellation waits for background probe before releasing shared lock, plus serialization, fixed error messages and secret omission. They release fake probe deterministically; they do not prove finite shutdown if real threaded network work never completes. Digest routing/list status use fake scheduler/storage. No reset transaction, administrator authorization or malformed command argument coverage appears in this module. Read only this step, not executed; prior31 selected unit passes unchanged.

Twitter adapter selects newest source-order IDs then reverses selected subset for processing; default max_new_items1 can intentionally skip older unseen IDs when cursor advances to newest. On detail failure across all mirrors it breaks and retains last successful cursor, positive partial-failure behavior within selected subset. ID selection stops at first non-new ID and assumes descending timeline order. Text reads remain unbounded. Media fetch caps64MiB and rejects truncated body; cache key is URL SHA256, not content equality/version. Existing any-extension cache file is trusted/touched without length/hash revalidation; deterministic .tmp path races across same URL writers. Cleanup512MiB occurs before item downloads, not a reserved hard cap, and never cleans .tmp files. Cache ownership filtering/lease protections absent. Media failures propagate to detail retry/cursor hold. No remote/media downloads or cleanup executed.

Pinned scheduler does implement five-field cron with wildcards, ranges, lists and positive steps; invalid syntax falls back to interval. Earlier roadmap claiming cron is only reserved is stale.
Datetime matcher combines day-of-month and weekday with AND. This is an implementation semantic requiring explicit contract rather than assuming compatibility with another cron implementation.

Search scans minute by minute up to366days synchronously. Valid but impossible dates or next occurrence beyond horizon fall back to ordinary poll interval, which can execute a job at a nonmatching date.
Candidate begins at next minute; selected run sleeps relative delay with no persisted fire identity in this excerpt. DST/catchup and cross-instance guarantees need remaining source/tests.

Scheduler lines1..339 read: startup scans every asyncio task by generic rss-job-/rss-digest-* name prefixes without instance ownership. Isolated original-method control cancelled a separately-created task named rss-job-other-instance; real multi-plugin deployment impact remains unverified.

stop cancels registered tasks then awaits them suppressing only CancelledError. Isolated original-method control with an already-failed task raises RuntimeError before clearing task/lock registries. No bounded shutdown deadline in this method. Manual run_job_once tasks are not stored in the three loop task registries; remaining guarded methods require review.

Scheduler lines501..980 read. Digest collection catches archive failures in _archive_items then continues updating feed validators/bootstrap state; failed archival can therefore be acknowledged upstream. Source-level finding; persistence-failure integration not run.

Finally still records original OSError in in-memory snapshot and releases lock. No real storage/dispatcher/framework run.
